title: Digital Asset Accounting

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transaction records from a blockchain network against entries in an organization's internal accounting ledger.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: This page covers the accounting treatment and valuation methods for digital tokens that do not trade on an active market, including locked, restricted, and low-volume assets.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts is the practice of reviewing the code, state transitions, and economic logic of programs that execute on a blockchain.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recording, valuation, and reporting of assets held by DAOs, protocol treasuries, and other on-chain entities that manage funds through smart contracts and multisig wallets.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers how entities test and write down the carrying value of non-fungible tokens, digital collectibles, virtual land, in-game items, and similar one-of-a-kind intangible assets recorded on a blockchain.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the practice of recording and reporting blockchain based assets in financial statements. Artificial intelligence is now doing concrete work here, not theoretical. It matches on chain transaction records to internal ledger entries, flags missing or duplicated transfers, and drafts journal entries for token movements. It also reads smart contract code to identify functions that move funds or change ownership, and it compares those functions to what the contract claims to do. For unique digital assets, AI helps classify whether an item is a consumable, a collectible, or a financial asset under the relevant accounting standard. This is not prediction or trading, it is bookkeeping and audit support.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Reconciliation between a blockchain and a general ledger is the most mature area, because blockchains provide a complete, timestamped record that software can parse directly. Valuing illiquid tokens remains unsolved in any reliable way, since there is often no active market and AI cannot create a price where none exists. Auditing smart contracts is partially solved for known vulnerability patterns, but it cannot prove that a contract does what its authors intended. Decentralised treasury accounting is still early, because control and ownership are often spread across multisig wallets and governance votes, which do not map neatly to traditional custody. Impairment of unique digital assets is also difficult, because fair value may be unknowable and AI can only flag indicators, not measure the loss. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments, but that number says nothing about how many of those instruments have enough trading depth to support a defensible valuation.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to see how raw blockchain data becomes a trial balance should start with Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation. Valuing Illiquid Tokens explains why some tokens have no observable price and what methods are being attempted, while Auditing Smart Contracts covers the code level checks that AI can and cannot perform. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries moves from single assets to the problem of reporting funds controlled by a group rather than a company. Impairment of Unique Digital Assets closes the loop by asking what happens when those assets lose value and how a write down might be supported. Together the five pages move from data capture, to valuation, to code verification, to control, and finally to loss recognition.
